items.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: In the rhythm is the rhythm section you saw last night: Danny Mixon, Dave Gibson, and Gerald Cannon, if Earl May isn’t available.

ctx.x: Why [laughs] didn’t he tell me? William Lowe, a bass trombonist, and Bob Trowers, who came out of the Basie band with me. In the saxophone section I have Bruce Williams playing lead alto. Joe Ford is my regular second alto saxophonist. Bill Saxton, who’s a stalwart and veteran of one of the earlier Loud Minority bands. I have a lady playing baritone saxophone, as I told you earlier, Fostina Dixon. On the other tenor saxophone is Keith Loftus, another young giant that I plucked from the New School. In the rhythm…
What about your mid-size -- you have two mid-size bands, don’t you? Or just one?

items.title: Frank Foster and Bill Hughes interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Schenectady, New York, March 28, 1995
items.q: it’s a pianist by the name of Danny Mixon who played with me in my small group

ctx.x: What’s this thing about Papa Foss? I heard that song the other day.

That’s what the thing about Papa— it’s a pianist by the name of Danny Mixon who played with me in my small group and he’s a Loud Minority so you know he’s Spacetakovitch, like we all were, and he composed this song called “Papa Foss” [scats]. So he didn’t have any lyrics to it. So my wife Cecelia and I got together and we put the lyrics to this song. and I sold Carmen Bradford on the idea of singing it. And of course it put me out front, you know, “standing out in front of it is Papa Foss, been out in front of it…
Yeah, they’ve been playing it in Syracuse.
